clue.text: Musical series coming back was in fashion

indicators.note: coming back tells us to read the assembled pieces in the opposite direction

parts.note: to have worn clothes is to have been in them
ton is an old word for the height of fashion

explanation.surface: A run of shows returns to the stage, having once been all the rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns WORETON round as one run. A note row (tone row) is the ordered series of twelve notes in serial music.
explanation.definitionFit: In twelve-tone composition the fixed ordering of pitches is called a note row or tone row.

clue.text: Kid holding record for one colourfully robed

indicators.note: holding means one piece contains the other inside it

parts.note: to kid is to tease, or josh
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A youngster clutching a disc, perhaps wearing bright clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but it is the verb meaning to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Joseph was given a coat of many colours by his father Jacob.

clue.text: Freedom given to one side to contribute

parts.note: play is freedom of movement, as in a rope with some play in it
A is one, the indefinite article
a part is one side in a dispute

explanation.surface: Liberty given to one faction so it can chip in.
explanation.definitionFit: To play a part in something is an idiom for contributing to it.

clue.text: City's wingers in uproar stop playing?

indicators.note: the wingers of a word are its two outer letters, like players on the flanks

parts.note: to ban a player is to stop them from playing

explanation.surface: Fans of a city club rioting over whether matches should be halted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City's' looks like part of a football surface but is the definition, an adjective meaning of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban is the adjective describing things belonging to a town or city.

clue.text: Poor journalist embraced by old marshal

indicators.note: embraced by means the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: An impoverished reporter hugged by an elderly army commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy and poor are synonyms for lacking money or essentials.

clue.text: Spare blanket to remove from seat?

parts.note: spare means left over, extra
a throw is a light blanket or bedspread

explanation.surface: An extra rug to clear off a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: The seat is a seat of power: to overthrow a ruler is to unseat them.
explanation.definitionFit: Overthrowing a government or ruler removes it from its seat of power.

clue.text: Ok to take centre in once that's co-opted onto team

indicators.note: something co-opted is taken in, so the following words go inside
centre in picks out the middle letters of the word once

parts.note: taken as written
XI is a team of eleven, as in cricket or football

explanation.surface: A recruit is approved to play in the middle for the side he was drafted into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ok' is the definition, an adjective here: safe, harmless. 'centre in' takes the middle two letters of once, and 'that's co-opted' puts the next words inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something non-toxic is harmless, safe, and so all right or okay.

clue.text: Single sportsperson's pad made possible?

parts.note: in cricket a run can be scored after the ball strikes the batter's pad or body rather than the bat

explanation.surface: A lone athlete's flat became affordable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' looks like an unmarried person and 'pad' a flat; in cricket a single is one run and a pad is leg protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg bye is an extra run scored when the ball deflects off the batter's body, not the bat.

clue.text: German town where father in fact has returned

indicators.note: has returned tells us the assembled letters are read backwards
in places father inside the word for fact

parts.note: what is fact is true
FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A town in Germany where Dad has really come home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has returned' reverses the whole container. Erfurt is in Thuringia, central Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Erfurt is the capital city of the German state of Thuringia.

clue.text: Number of customers in shop decline to pay upfront

indicators.note: upfront puts the paying word before the declining word

parts.note: to foot a bill is to pay it
a fall is a decline

explanation.surface: Retail visitor numbers drop when customers must pay in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Footfall is the retail term for the number of people entering a shop.

clue.text: Wash dirt off around end of teatime with this?

definitions.text: Wash dirt off around end of teatime with this?

indicators.note: around means the anagram goes round the final letter
off suggests the letters are spoilt and rearranged
end of picks the last letter of teatime

explanation.surface: After tea, use this to clean up the plates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges WASHDIRT to DISHWATR, which goes 'around' E, the last letter of teatime.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishwater is the water used for washing the plates after a meal.

clue.text: Second lot of ashes perhaps to put on weeds?

parts.note: MO, a moment, is a second
an urn holds a person's ashes; it is also the cricket trophy the Ashes

explanation.surface: A cricket follow-up series in the garden before the weeding.
explanation.walkthrough: Widow's weeds are mourning clothes, so putting them on is what a mourner does.
explanation.definitionFit: To grieve is traditionally marked by wearing black widow's weeds.

clue.text: Belief, fading every so often, died in some

indicators.note: fading every so often means letters disappear at regular intervals, leaving alternate ones

explanation.surface: A faith that waned now and then has died among a few.
explanation.definitionFit: Deism is a belief in a creator God who does not intervene in the world.

clue.text: Quantity of work to do in unfinished old stone, we understand?

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for do in loses its final letter

parts.note: to do someone in is to kill them

indicators.note: we understand means the word for stone is taken by ear

parts.note: a jewel is a precious stone

explanation.surface: Murdering someone with an ancient rock takes some effort, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts KILL to KIL; 'we understand' turns JEWEL into its sound-alike, the energy unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Work in physics is measured in energy units, and a kilojoule is a thousand joules.

clue.text: Wren maybe briefly met by the Queen's old physician

indicators.note: briefly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Jenny wren is a traditional name for the bird
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A naval servicewoman meets the monarch's doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wren' looks like a Women's Royal Naval Service member; it is the bird. Edward Jenner pioneered smallpox vaccination.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Jenner was an eighteenth-century English doctor who developed vaccination.

clue.text: Minister's habit to say what's not required

indicators.note: to say signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a surplice is a white vestment worn by clergy

explanation.surface: A clergyman's robe, used to declare what is unwanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplus is an excess, the amount beyond what is needed.

clue.text: Sister hiding nose job? Fiancé didn't mean to joke

indicators.note: hiding means one piece is concealed within the other

parts.note: a sister in religion is a nun
a nose job is an operation, abbreviated OP
your intended is the person you are engaged to

explanation.surface: A nun secretly had cosmetic surgery, and her fiancé meant no jest.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said when a remark accidentally contains wordplay the speaker did not mean.

clue.text: Denied article being given up in part for this?

definitions.text: Denied article being given up in part for this?

indicators.note: given up in a down answer means read from bottom to top
in part means the letters are only some of those in the words

explanation.surface: An item refused because it was surrendered as part-payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in part' takes NIEDART from deNIED ARTicle; 'being given up' turns it to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is an old item handed over as part-payment for a new one.

clue.text: Touching topless woman on hand

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: Moving scenes of an undressed woman nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ready is available and at hand when needed.

clue.text: Does it matter awfully how fat one is over time?

indicators.note: is over places the first piece above the second in a down answer
awfully suggests the letters are badly jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it truly matters how heavy they have become.
explanation.definitionFit: The retort is a dismissive way of asking why something should matter.

clue.text: The writer in French Resistance storing too much in notepad

indicators.note: storing means the pieces hold another inside

parts.note: je is French for I, the writer
OTT is over the top
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A Resistance fighter stashing excess documents in a pad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French Resistance' suggests the wartime movement; here it splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A jotter is a small pad for scribbled notes.

clue.text: Weightlifting exercise assessment shorter than the others?

parts.note: the squat is a lifting exercise with the bar on the shoulders
a test is an assessment

explanation.surface: A gym exam to see who is the stubbiest.
explanation.definitionFit: Squat means short and stocky, and this is its superlative form.

clue.text: Boxer collecting black ointment in local dishes

indicators.note: collecting means one piece takes another inside

parts.note: pug is short for pugilist, a boxer
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a rub is an ointment massaged in

explanation.surface: A fighter picking up dark balm from the nearby plates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' is British for one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is a neighbourhood pub, and its dishes are pub food.

clue.text: Swede served with mint over fire for people

indicators.note: over places the mint word above the fire word in a down answer

parts.note: mint means brand new
fire means passion or zeal
Anders is a typical Swedish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian served a mint dish cooked above flames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swede' suggests the vegetable; it is a Swedish name.
explanation.definitionFit: New Zealanders are the people of New Zealand.

clue.text: One female in eight roughly was a moron

indicators.note: roughly suggests a loose rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A woman in a rowing crew behaved stupidly.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a rowing crew of eight rowers.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight is a racing boat of eight rowers, so a female rower is one member.

clue.text: Name associated with streams and plain

parts.note: of shows association or belonging
rills are small streams

explanation.surface: A name linked with brooks and flat country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like a noun for flat land; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: No-frills describes something basic and unadorned.

clue.text: V necks set out for carnival

indicators.note: to neck is to swallow, so the first piece takes the other inside

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: V-necked tops laid out for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET to EST, which FIVE 'necks'.
explanation.definitionFit: Festive and carnival as adjectives both describe a celebratory atmosphere.

clue.text: Recalled large articles about America repeatedly and predictably

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read in reverse
about means the articles go around the rest

parts.note: A and A are two indefinite articles

indicators.note: repeatedly means the piece appears twice

parts.note: US is America

explanation.surface: Big items brought back concerning the United States over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: L plus A, USUS, A gives LAUSUSA, which 'Recalled' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: As usual means in the expected way, just as one would predict.

clue.text: Irish writer to feed rumour at the outset

parts.note: to stoke a fire is to feed it with fuel

indicators.note: at the outset picks the first letter of rumour

explanation.surface: An author from Ireland starting gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker, author of Dracula, was born in Dublin.

clue.text: System of changes Barbara Shaw created for one

definitions.meaning: in bell-ringing, methods rung on eight bells are called by this name
Shaw's play features a Salvation Army officer, Barbara, whose rank is in the title

explanation.surface: A reorganisation devised by a playwright for an actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Major is a bell-ringing class on eight bells and an army rank in Shaw's play title.
